sourceObjectiveEnglish: Give directions on campus: Use en for in/on/at as context requires.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Ayudar a un visitante with a patient classmate. Practice give directions on campus. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: Use en for in/on/at as context requires. Cerca de, lejos de, delante de and detrás de locate things. De + el becomes del.

examples.es: La biblioteca está al lado del café.
examples.en: The library is next to the café.

examples.es: La sala de estudio está detrás de la biblioteca.
examples.en: The study room is behind the library.

cards.decisionNote: Spanish mochila is feminine, while French sac à dos is masculine; downstream article and possessive choices need contextual review.
Source clase groups a class session with a classroom; French cours, classe and salle de classe are distinct.
Spanish está marks condition/location; French est also expresses identity, so an isolated card changes the contrast.
Spanish el marks masculine singular; French le can elide and must be linked to a noun.
Spanish la groups feminine article, object it and person her; one French la face hides role and elision.
Spanish una is feminine singular; French une depends on the noun selected.
Source en groups in/on/at; French dans, sur, à and au depend on the location phrase.
Spanish mi is gender-neutral; French mon/ma/mes depend on the possessed noun and phonology.
Spanish de groups of/from and contracts with el; French de/du/des and locative de need phrase context.

cards.sourceSpanish: La biblioteca está al lado del café.
cards.sourceEnglish: The library is next to the café.
cards.proposedFrench: La bibliothèque est à côté du café.

cards.sourceSpanish: La sala de estudio está detrás de la biblioteca.
cards.sourceEnglish: The study room is behind the library.
cards.proposedFrench: La salle d’étude est derrière la bibliothèque.

cards.sourceSpanish: Hay una mesa delante de la ventana.
cards.sourceEnglish: There is a table in front of the window.
cards.proposedFrench: Il y a une table devant la fenêtre.

cards.sourceSpanish: Mi mochila está debajo de esa mesa.
cards.sourceEnglish: My backpack is under that table.
cards.proposedFrench: Mon sac à dos est sous cette table.
cards.decisionNote: Source feminine mochila becomes masculine sac à dos; mon agrees with sac, not the speaker.

cards.sourceSpanish: La clase está cerca de la puerta principal.
cards.sourceEnglish: The classroom is near the main door.
cards.proposedFrench: La salle de classe est près de la porte principale.
cards.decisionNote: Source la clase means the classroom here; salle de classe preserves that room sense.

cards.sourceSpanish: El parque está lejos de este edificio.
cards.sourceEnglish: The park is far from this building.
cards.proposedFrench: Le parc est loin de ce bâtiment.

cards.sourceSpanish: La clase está en el segundo piso.
cards.sourceEnglish: The classroom is on the second floor.
cards.proposedFrench: La salle de classe est au deuxième étage.
cards.decisionNote: Source segundo piso is the second floor; French deuxième étage is a conditional locale choice.

archivedRedesign.title: Guider vers une entrée de remplacement
archivedRedesign.scene: L’entrée habituelle de la bibliothèque est fermée. Un visiteur doit suivre un trajet différent et reformuler les étapes.
archivedRedesign.reason: The archived replacement-entrance guidance changes the source campus locations and objective; it cannot inherit this lesson's saved positions or recordings.

sourceDecisions: The source Spanish objective uses en as in/on/at by context; French requires phrase-specific à, dans, sur and au, not a slash string scored as one answer.
Source cerca de, lejos de, delante de, detrás de and de + el contraction need a French spatial-language sequence with direct grammatical examples.
Source class/classroom, mochila/sac à dos and gendered articles/possessives need contextual dictionary and saved-item decisions.
The source is an elementary directions lesson placed at Master 15; qualified curriculum review must decide progression without silently changing the stable progress identity.
